name: glide-mark
title: Gliding block
description: One block for a whole list: it glides to the row under the pointer in 200ms and rests on the picked one when the pointer leaves, so moving down a list is one movement.
use_for: Lists read by moving down them, such as prices, suggestions and the docs' sidebar.
never: A row of separate hover fills in the same list
Touch screens: it follows the pointer only
body: `useGlideMark(list, rest)` measures the list's `[data-glide-row]` children: call `point(i)` on pointer enter and focus, `leave()` on pointer leave, and `settle()` after the pick changes. `rest` returns the row to rest on, or null to hide. Draw the block with `<GlideMark :mark :instant />` first in the list, and lift the rows above it (`relative z-1`).

files.content:
<script setup lang="ts">
// The gliding block itself (console2.css .v2-rowmark): the paper behind the row useGlideMark points at, moving on
// transform and height in 200ms on the strong ease-out, and placed without a glide the first time. Put it first inside
// the list (which is position: relative) and give the rows a z-index above it. Reduced motion places it at once.
defineProps<{ mark: { y: number, h: number } | null, instant?: boolean }>()
</script>

<template>
  <span data-ds="glide-mark" v-if="mark" class="ds-rowmark" :data-instant="instant || undefined" :style="{ transform: `translateY(${mark.y}px)`, height: `${mark.h}px` }" aria-hidden="true" />
</template>

<style>
.ds-rowmark { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; left: 0; z-index: 0; background: var(--ds-color-surface-subtle); pointer-events: none; transition: transform var(--ds-duration-enter) var(--ds-easing-out), height var(--ds-duration-enter) var(--ds-easing-out); }
.ds-rowmark[data-instant] { transition: none; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-rowmark { transition: none; } }
</style>
